findings.description: Critical: Tasks 3.2 and 3.7 invent a 'Step 10 phase-results assembly' and claim Step 11 contains two Phase Results blocks. In skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md, Step 10 is Teardown; the illustrative `### Phase Results` sketch is under Step 11; the heredoc that writes `$REPORT_FILE` with `## Phase Results` and placeholder `<phase results from Step 10>` is under Step 12 Persist Report. There is no Step 10 assembly block to edit or assert, so the dual-edit/dual-assert instructions are not implementable as written and risk editing only the sketch.
findings.resolution: Rewrite 3.2/3.7 against the real structure: require a `Choices:` row in (1) the Step 11 sketch and (2) explicit fill instructions for the Step 12 heredoc placeholder (or an adjacent assembly snippet that produces those lines). Have 3.7 assert both loci, not a nonexistent Step 10 assembly.

findings.description: Critical: Task 3.6 claims skill-workflow.12 by invoking 'the CLI' with a single `<base>..<head>` argument and asserting base/head were derived from it. `skills/audit-choices/scripts/run_audit.py` has no such arity — it requires `--change-id`, `--base-sha`, and `--head-sha` separately — and range resolution lives only as agent instructions in `audit-choices/SKILL.md` Step 1. Under the proposal's no-driver-change constraint, that pytest assertion has no existing entry point to call; a test that fabricates `change_id=range:...` still fails the task's own anti-bypass rule.
findings.resolution: Either (a) add a small pure range-arg parser (outside persistence) that 3.6 can unit-test and that SKILL.md Step 1 must call, or (b) move scenario 12 coverage to a 3.7-style content pin of the Arguments/Step 1 range form and narrow the scenario/task to match what Phase 2 actually shipped.

findings.description: Nit: design.md Risks still says 'Scenario 11 asserts only the recorded `change_id` and the exit code' for the standalone `range:` ledger-path quirk. After F7 renumbering, standalone range is skill-workflow.12; skill-workflow.11 is 'Absent or empty ledger is silent at the gates'.
findings.resolution: Replace 'Scenario 11' with 'Scenario 12' (skill-workflow.12) in that Risks bullet so the ordinal matches tasks.md's scenario key table.

findings.description: Nit: proposal.md Selected Approach says `tasks.md` encodes a dependency graph where '3.6 depends on 3.0–3.3', but tasks.md lists 3.6 Dependencies as 3.0 only and explicitly states it does not depend on 3.1–3.3 (scenario 8 stays on 3.1+3.7). plan-findings.md's parallelizability graph still shows `3.0 → {3.2, 3.3} → 3.6`.
findings.resolution: Align proposal.md (and the plan-findings parallelizability summary) with tasks.md: 3.6 depends only on 3.0; 3.7 depends on 3.1–3.3.

findings.description: Nit: Scenario 'Absent or empty ledger is silent at the gates' requires that both validate-feature and cleanup-feature presentations 'SHALL state that no open choices exist'. Tasks 3.2/3.7 pin validate-feature to `○ Choices: no ledger` and `✓ Choices: <n> entries, 0 needs-user`, which never use that phrase; only cleanup uses `no open choices`. Spec SHALL and task strings disagree.
findings.resolution: Either loosen the scenario to allow gate-specific equivalent wording (and cite the ○/✓ forms), or change the validate-feature row strings so both gates literally state that no open choices exist.

findings.description: Nit: F2's load-bearing 'commit only when entry payload changed' rule (compare `choices.json` with `generated_at`/`run_id` stripped; restore both files when only the volatile header moved) is specified in task 3.1/design F2 but task 3.7 does not assert that wording — only VENDOR_REVIEW, the skip line, both-files-present, and the two `git add` pathspecs. A SKILL.md rewrite could drop the payload comparison, emit content-free `chore(choices):` commits every run, and still pass 3.7.
findings.resolution: Extend 3.7's iterate-on-implementation assertions to require the entry-payload comparison / `generated_at`+`run_id` strip / restore-on-header-only wording from F2.

findings.description: Optional: Task 3.6 lists skill-workflow.2 ('Missing ledger does not block archive') under its driver e2e via 'absence does not block (2)'. Parent/canonical scenario 2's THEN is that validation must not fail and archive must proceed without a ledger — behavior this fixture-repo driver run never exercises.
findings.resolution: Drop skill-workflow.2 from 3.6's scenario list (keep absence covered under scenario 11's reader/gate silence), or add an explicit archive/validate non-failure assertion if that coverage is still desired here.
